day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter train) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.50). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation canal walk: Stroll along the Prinsengracht and Herengracht canals near your hotel. Explore the Jordaan neighborhood — browse local boutiques, street art, and admire the iconic 17th-century canal houses. Stop at the Westerkerk (free exterior viewing) for great canal views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) area on foot — a charming grid of specialty shops and cozy cafés. End the evening with a relaxed walk along the lit canals as dusk falls over Amsterdam.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack or coffee at Schiphol Airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a local broodjeszaak (sandwich shop) near Centraal Station — budget €4–7 for a hearty Dutch broodje (sandwich).
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant or Foodhallen (indoor food market) — try stamppot or Dutch bitterballen. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol for €7.50 (€2.50 card fee + €5 credit) — it covers trams, buses, and metro throughout your stay. Validate every time you board and exit.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Open at 09:00 — arrive early to beat the crowds. Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch) and Vermeer (The Milkmaid). Budget ~3 hours. Admission: €22.50 (book online in advance to save time and guarantee entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Rijksmuseum, walk through the beautiful Museumplein (free) and relax by the iconic 'I Amsterdam' letters area. Then head to the nearby Vondelpark (free entry) — Amsterdam's most famous park — for a peaceful afternoon stroll along the ponds and gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Tram back toward the canal belt. Take a self-guided evening canal walk along the Leidsegracht and Keizersgracht — the canals are beautifully lit at dusk. Browse the Albert Heijn supermarket for affordable snacks or a picnic near the water.

meals.breakfast: Bakkerij Hartog or a local Albert Heijn supermarket — fresh stroopwafels, coffee, and a croissant for under €5.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick lunch at Museumplein food stalls or Loetje aan het Museumplein — Dutch kroket sandwich (broodje kroket) for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Café Loetje or De Peper (vegan, pay-what-you-can community dinner, ~€8–10) near Vondelpark — filling and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum tickets online at rijksmuseum.nl at least a few days ahead — weekend slots sell out fast. The museum is a 15-minute tram ride (Tram 2 or 12) from Canal House Amsterdam.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: One of Amsterdam's most moving and essential experiences. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Tickets MUST be booked online months in advance (€16 per person) — Sunday slots are extremely limited. Arrive 10 minutes early. Duration: ~1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Anne Frank House, explore the Jordaan neighborhood market scene — visit the Noordermarkt (open Sunday mornings until ~15:00) for organic produce, vintage goods, and local crafts. Then stroll along the Brouwersgracht, considered one of Amsterdam's most picturesque canals.
day_by_day.evening: Van Gogh Museum Experience: Book a late-afternoon/early evening slot (open until 18:00 on Sundays, sometimes extended). Discover the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Admission: €22 (book online at vangoghmuseum.nl). Budget ~2 hours.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 near the Anne Frank House — famous for their apple pie (appeltaart, €4.50) and coffee. A local Sunday tradition.
meals.lunch: Noordermarkt food stalls — try Dutch poffertjes (mini pancakes) or a fresh stroopwafel for €3–5.
meals.dinner: Foodhallen Amsterdam (indoor street food market) — wide variety of cuisines at €8–14 per dish. Great atmosphere and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are the hardest to get in Amsterdam — book as early as possible at annefrank.org. If sold out, join the small daily release of same-day tickets online at 09:00 sharp. Van Gogh Museum is a 10-minute walk from the Anne Frank House via tram.

day_by_day.morning: Private Canal Boat Tour: Glide through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring on a guided boat tour, passing iconic 17th-century canal houses, drawbridges, and hidden gardens. Morning departures typically offer calmer waterways. Duration: ~1.5–2 hours. Note: 'Private' tours are premium — consider a shared group boat tour (e.g., Blue Boat Company or Lovers Canal Cruises) for €15–18 to keep it budget-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Amsterdam's free and low-cost gems: Visit the Amsterdam Museum (check for free entry days) or the Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard with a free chapel, tucked away from tourist crowds. Then browse the Spui Square book market (Mondays, free) for secondhand Dutch and English books.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the NDSM Wharf (free ferry from Centraal Station, ~15 min) — a former shipyard turned creative hub with street art, urban culture, and great views of the IJ waterfront. Free to explore. Return by ferry in the evening.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast if included, or grab a fresh bagel and coffee from Bagels & Beans (~€6–8) near the canal belt.
meals.lunch: Grab a Dutch herring (haring) from a street haringkar (herring cart) near Spui — a true Amsterdam experience for just €3–4.
meals.dinner: Surinamese restaurant like Roopram Roti or Warung Spang Makandra in the Pijp neighborhood — generous portions of roti and curry for €8–12. Amsterdam's Surinamese food scene is world-class and very affordable.

day_by_day.notes: The free GVB ferry from Amsterdam Centraal (behind the station) to NDSM Wharf runs every 30 minutes and is a scenic mini-cruise in itself. Wear comfortable shoes for the wharf exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam — one of the world's oldest botanical gardens (est. 1638), with over 6,000 plant species. A peaceful and beautiful way to spend a final morning. Admission: €11.50 (discounted with Iamsterdam City Card if purchased). Open from 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Historical Museum and the Portuguese Synagogue area (Waterlooplein) — the synagogue exterior is free to admire. Browse the Waterlooplein Flea Market (open Monday–Saturday, free entry) for vintage finds, souvenirs, and Dutch memorabilia. Great spot to pick up affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Final canal farewell: Take a slow tram or walk back along the Amstel River and the Keizersgracht for one last golden-hour view of Amsterdam's canals. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Check out logistics with your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Café de Jaren near Waterlooplein — classic Dutch breakfast with eggs, cheese, and coffee for €8–11. Beautiful canal-side terrace.
meals.lunch: Waterlooplein market food stalls or Broodjeszaak Joodse Buurt — affordable Dutch sandwiches and soups for €5–7.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a final dinner at In de Waag (inside a historic 15th-century city gate) or keep it budget with a classic Dutch pannenkoeken (pancake) at Pancakes Amsterdam — pancakes from €10–13, filling and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early the next morning, confirm your train or shuttle to Schiphol the night before. The Sprinter train from Centraal to Schiphol runs 24/7 and costs ~€5.50. Leave at least 2.5 hours before your flight for security and check-in.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Rijksmuseum Visit
experiences.description: Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt and Vermeer. The stunning building itself is a work of art, and the collection spans 800 years of Dutch history including the famous Night Watch painting.

experiences.description: Stroll through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood, sampling Dutch street food including stroopwafels, raw herring (haring), and artisan cheeses at local markets. day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.50), then taxi or tram to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a self-guided stroll along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — Join the guided food and canal walk through Amsterdam's most charming neighborhood. Sample Dutch street food: stroopwafels, bitterballen, and fresh herring. Admire the narrow canal houses, hidden courtyards (hofjes), and local boutiques. This is a perfect gentle introduction to the city after a travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Leidseplein square area for a relaxed dinner and drinks. Watch the city come alive on a Saturday evening — street performers, terrace cafés, and golden-hour light on the canals.

meals.breakfast: Eat at Schiphol Airport before landing or grab a quick bite at Amsterdam Centraal — try Stach Food for fresh sandwiches and salads (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings are included during the Jordaan Food & Canal Walk — supplement with a fresh herring broodje (sandwich) from a canal-side haringkar (herring cart) for ~€4.
meals.dinner: Café de Reiger in the Jordaan — a beloved Dutch brown café serving seasonal Dutch-French bistro dishes. Mains €18–26. Cozy, candlelit, and very local.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The Jordaan walk covers ground very close to Canal House Amsterdam, so no long transit needed. Book the Jordaan Food & Canal Walk in advance if possible. Confirm hotel check-in time is before 13:00 arrival; if not, luggage storage is available at Amsterdam Centraal.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Arrive at opening (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Highlights include Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and the stunning Cuypers Library. Pre-book timed entry tickets online (~€22.50 adults).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Located just steps from the Rijksmuseum on Museumplein, head there after lunch. Discover the world's largest Van Gogh collection: 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and hundreds of drawings and letters. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Tickets ~€22 adults — must be pre-booked online as walk-ins are rarely available.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the elegant Oud-Zuid neighborhood back toward the hotel. Stop at the Albert Cuyp Market area (closes around 17:30 on Sundays — check seasonal hours) or simply enjoy the canal views along the Keizersgracht at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby — try Café Toussaint on Bosboom Toussaintstraat for a classic Dutch breakfast with eggs, bread, and coffee (€10–15).
meals.lunch: Café Cobra on Museumplein — right between the two museums. Sandwiches, soups, and salads with terrace seating overlooking the 'I amsterdam' area (€12–18). Great for a quick, quality mid-museum break.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Blauw on Amstelveenseweg — outstanding Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table), a Dutch-colonial tradition. A must-try in Amsterdam. Set menus €28–35 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Museum Day — both museums are within 5 minutes' walk of each other on Museumplein. Book BOTH tickets online well in advance; the Van Gogh Museum frequently sells out days ahead, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable shoes. The Museumplein lawn is lovely for a short rest between museums if weather permits.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — This is Amsterdam's most emotionally powerful experience. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid for over two years during WWII. The museum is deeply moving and historically essential. Entry is strictly by timed ticket only (~€16 adults) — book online months in advance as this is the hardest ticket in Amsterdam to secure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After the weight of the Anne Frank House, a private guided canal boat tour is a perfect contrast. Glide through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring, passing 17th-century merchant houses, drawbridges, and hidden houseboats. Your guide will share the history of the Golden Age that built this city. Tours typically depart from near the Prinsengracht, very close to the Anne Frank House.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to explore independently. Wander the Nine Streets (De 9 Straatjes) — a grid of charming cross-streets between the main canals, lined with vintage shops, galleries, and cozy bars. Perfect for souvenir shopping and a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam (if included) or visit Winkel 43 on the Noordermarkt for their legendary apple pie and coffee — a true Amsterdam institution (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Grab a Dutch broodje (sandwich) from Broodje Bert near the Jordaan — classic Dutch deli sandwiches with local cheeses and meats (€6–10). Eat canal-side.
meals.dinner: Restaurant 't Smalle — a historic canal house café/restaurant on the Egelantiersgracht in the Jordaan. Classic Dutch and European cuisine in a stunning 18th-century interior. Mains €19–27.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House ticket situation is critical — check the official annefrank.org site regularly as a small number of tickets are released daily at 9:00 AM CET. If tickets are unavailable, consider the Jewish Historical Museum as an alternative. The canal boat tour and Anne Frank House are within easy walking distance of each other and from Canal House Amsterdam.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Zaanse Schans — Take a 20-minute train from Amsterdam Centraal to this open-air museum village featuring working windmills, traditional wooden houses, a clog workshop, and a cheese farm. Arrive early (~9:30 AM) before tour groups arrive. Entry to the village is free; individual attractions charge small fees (€4–8 each). A quintessentially Dutch experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Amsterdam by 14:00. Spend the afternoon exploring the Eastern Docklands (Java-eiland and KNSM-eiland) — Amsterdam's modern architectural showcase along the IJ waterfront. A striking contrast to the historic canal ring. Alternatively, visit the FOAM Photography Museum on the Keizersgracht if you prefer staying central (~€15 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Rembrandtplein square — one of Amsterdam's main entertainment hubs. Have a pre-dinner drink at a terrace café watching the square's energy, then head to dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departing — pick up fresh stroopwafels and coffee from a bakery near Amsterdam Centraal station. Albert Heijn supermarket in the station is a budget-friendly option (€5–8).
meals.lunch: At Zaanse Schans — try the on-site pancake restaurant 'De Kraai' for traditional Dutch pannenkoeken (pancakes, both sweet and savory, €10–15). A classic Dutch lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Proeflokaal Wynand Fockink — start with Dutch jenever (gin) tasting at this historic 1679 tasting house near Rembrandtplein, then dinner at Scheepskameel in the Eastern Docklands or Brasserie Harkema (Nes street) for French-Dutch cuisine. Mains €20–28.

day_by_day.notes: For Zaanse Schans, take the Sprinter train from Amsterdam Centraal to Zaandijk Zaanse Schans station (direct, ~17 min, €4 each way). Alternatively, a direct bus runs seasonally. The village gets very crowded after 11 AM, so an early start is strongly recommended. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy near the windmills.

day_by_day.morning: Final canal morning — Rent a pedal boat or kayak on the Prinsengracht or Amstel River for a DIY canal experience (€15–20/hour). This is a wonderful, active way to see the city from water level on your last morning. Alternatively, take a leisurely walk along the Amstel River toward the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) for classic Amsterdam photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration and shopping — Visit the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market) on the Singel canal for tulip bulbs and Dutch souvenirs. Browse the boutiques along the Utrechtsestraat or Haarlemmerstraat for local design and gifts. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a memorable final meal. Head to the Jordaan or De Pijp neighborhood for a relaxed, celebratory dinner before heading to the airport or resting for an early next-day departure.

meals.breakfast: Café Papeneiland on the Prinsengracht — Amsterdam's oldest café (1642), serving coffee and apple pie in a gorgeous canal-side setting. A perfect final Amsterdam morning (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market in De Pijp — Amsterdam's largest street market. Grab fresh stroopwafels, Dutch cheese samples, raw herring, and a fresh juice from the stalls (€10–15 total). Vibrant, colorful, and very local.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Greetje — Amsterdam's finest modern Dutch cuisine, celebrating seasonal and traditional Dutch ingredients in creative ways. A perfect farewell dinner. Mains €26–34. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is early on Day 6, pack the night before and arrange a taxi or early tram to Amsterdam Centraal for the Schiphol Airport Express. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Canal House Amsterdam may offer luggage storage if you need to check out early but have time before your flight. Keep your OV-chipkaart (transit card) loaded for easy airport travel.

meals.dinner: Restaurant Vinkeles — Michelin-starred tasting menu with optional wine pairing; reserve the chef's table for an intimate experience

day_by_day.evening: Aperitifs at the rooftop bar of Hotel V Nesplein for panoramic city views, followed by dinner at Ciel Bleu, the two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura, offering breathtaking views of Amsterdam alongside exquisite contemporary cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, and barista coffee served in the elegant dining room
meals.lunch: Grand Café Cobra in Museumplein — sophisticated café cuisine with terrace seating, ideally located between the two museums
meals.dinner: Ciel Bleu at Hotel Okura — two-Michelin-star tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine flight; request a window table for skyline views

day_by_day.evening: Visit the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) for curated luxury shopping — independent boutiques, antique dealers, and designer concept stores. meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam, followed by a specialty coffee at Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters — one of Amsterdam's finest specialty cafés, located in the Jordaan
meals.lunch: Grazing lunch during the Jordaan Food Walk — curated tastings from market stalls and local purveyors included in the tour
meals.dinner: Restaurant Breda — inventive Dutch cuisine with seasonal ingredients, elegant atmosphere, and an exceptional natural wine list

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House is a 5-minute walk from Canal House Amsterdam. Timed tickets are non-negotiable and sell out months ahead — confirm booking before departure. The Jordaan walk flows naturally from the Anne Frank House location.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning canal kayak or paddleboard experience on the quieter inner canals — a unique, active perspective of the city before the tourist crowds arrive. Alternatively, arrange a private art tour of Amsterdam's world-class gallery district, including the Foam Photography Museum and the Stedelijk Museum of modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day excursion to Keukenhof Gardens (seasonal — typically open through mid-May) or a private guided visit to a traditional Dutch windmill village such as Zaanse Schans, accessible by private car in under 30 minutes. Experience authentic Dutch heritage, wooden clog workshops, and scenic countryside landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Amsterdam for a relaxing evening. Sunset drinks aboard a private moored canal boat with a personal butler and champagne service arranged through the hotel. Dinner at Rijsel, a beloved Amsterdam institution serving exceptional Flemish rotisserie chicken and seasonal dishes in a warm, convivial setting.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service at Canal House Amsterdam — continental spread delivered to your suite with fresh-squeezed juices and pastries from Vlaamsch Broodhuys bakery
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed at Keukenhof Gardens or Zaanse Schans, or dine at Restaurant De Hoop op d'Swarte Walvis in Zaandam — a historic waterside restaurant with excellent Dutch cuisine
meals.dinner: Rijsel — arrive early to secure a table; no reservations taken, so the hotel concierge may assist with priority arrangements

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Keukenhof opening dates — the gardens typically close in mid-May. If closed, Zaanse Schans is an excellent alternative. Arrange private car hire through the hotel for the day excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy an indulgent late breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam. Take a slow, reflective walk along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals, admiring the Golden Bend (Gouden Bocht) — the most prestigious stretch of canal houses in the city, home to the Amsterdam Museum of the Canals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along P.C. Hooftstraat — Amsterdam's premier designer shopping street featuring Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Chanel, and local Dutch luxury brands. Visit Moooi flagship store for iconic Dutch design. Optional: a final coffee and pastry at Patisserie Holtkamp, a legendary Amsterdam confectionery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Spectrum, the Michelin-starred restaurant at Hotel Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam, set within a row of six meticulously restored 17th-century canal houses. An unforgettable final evening celebrating Dutch culinary excellence. Arrange private chauffeur transfer to Schiphol Airport if departing tonight or early the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Extended late breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — full à la carte service with Dutch cheeses, smoked meats, fresh fruit, and house-baked breads
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café de Klepel in the Jordaan — a charming neighbourhood café with excellent sandwiches and salads, perfect for a relaxed final afternoon
meals.dinner: Spectrum at Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam — Michelin-starred multi-course tasting menu celebrating global flavors with Dutch craftsmanship; request the private dining room for an exclusive send-off

day_by_day.notes: Pack and arrange luggage storage with the hotel before the morning walk. Confirm departure transfer with the concierge. Spectrum dinner requires advance reservation — book as early as possible. A truly memorable conclusion to a luxury Amsterdam experience.
